authority_note: Additive research checkpoint only. companies/267260/latest.json, registry/companies.json, reviews/latest.json, canonical raw-data, baseline-lock and frozen deterministic outputs remain unchanged; current canonical authority remains the 2026-09-06-deep run until a separate reviewed promotion.
portfolio_context: Actual holding, tax basis and portfolio risk budget were not supplied in this run. No position size is invented and buy authorization remains false.
structural_thesis: Global grid replacement, electrification and AI data-center power demand are creating a multi-year shortage in large transformers, breakers and switchgear. HD Hyundai Electric has credible North American positioning through local Alabama production, 765kV capability, high-voltage qualification and a broad transmission-to-distribution portfolio, but the investment thesis still depends on maintaining pricing and capital efficiency after industry capacity expands.
current_finding: Harness-rule TTM diagnostics are approximately KRW4.337T revenue, KRW1.113T operating income, KRW0.850T net income and KRW0.983T operating cash flow. TTM disclosed PPE purchases were approximately KRW0.312T, leaving mechanical OCF-minus-PPE of KRW0.671T. This is not normalized owner FCF because intangible purchases, advance-payment timing, working capital and expansion economics are not fully normalized.
economic_finding: Q2 2026 revenue was KRW1.142T and operating profit KRW287.0B, for 25.1% operating margin. H1 orders reached $3.237B, about 76.7% of the $4.222B annual order target, while backlog reached $8.49B. A maximum KRW1.1212T framework agreement with a global Big Tech customer broadens the data-center proposition across power and distribution equipment, but only actual purchase orders should be treated as firm revenue evidence.
capital_and_survival: June 2026 company-defined deposits were approximately KRW1.010T versus borrowings of KRW114.5B, so financing dependence is low. The main capital question is return on the Ulsan and Alabama expansions: Alabama Plant 2 is intended to raise local transformer capacity by about 50%, but project-level after-tax incremental ROIC remains unproven until utilization, pricing and cash conversion are observed after ramp.
permanent_loss_case: Industry capacity catches up while AI-data-center financing and utility orders normalize; transformer lead times shorten and pricing power fades; the Big Tech framework converts into fewer purchase orders than headline maximums imply; Ulsan and Alabama expansions ramp below utilization targets; copper, tariff or logistics costs rise; working-capital benefits reverse; operating margin normalizes materially below the current mid-20s; and a valuation requiring long-duration double-digit growth de-rates even though the company remains profitable and solvent.
falsifiers: New-order pricing and backlog conversion weaken for multiple quarters while transformer lead times normalize materially.
Ulsan or Alabama capacity ramps with structurally lower utilization or after-tax returns below the 10% hurdle.
Operating cash flow per share persistently lags earnings growth after advances and working capital normalize.
A major North American customer materially reduces orders and diversified utility/data-center demand fails to offset the loss.
Power-equipment operating margin falls toward low-teens without an offsetting increase in capital turns or volume economics.
increase_evidence: At least two additional reporting periods showing backlog conversion, new-order pricing and OCF per share improving together.
Evidence that new Alabama/Ulsan capacity earns after-tax incremental returns above the 10% hurdle after ramp costs.
Actual purchase orders under the Big Tech framework convert into revenue and cash without abnormal working-capital or margin concessions.
Customer and regional concentration remain non-fatal while 765kV, distribution and data-center package wins broaden the mix.
Expectation gap becomes clearly favorable at a 10% required return; price decline alone is insufficient without business evidence.
sell_evidence: Backlog declines materially while book-to-bill and new-order pricing deteriorate across North America and other key regions.
Expansion assets generate low utilization or returns below the hurdle for multiple periods.
Cash conversion deteriorates structurally because advances reverse, receivables/inventory rise and OCF per share falls despite revenue growth.
Competitive capacity additions compress transformer pricing and normalized owner margin faster than volume growth offsets.
Any material accounting, governance or customer-value impairment triggers an immediate thesis rewrite regardless of price.

evidence: Q2 backlog reached $8.49B and H1 orders reached $3.237B while U.S. grid-equipment lead times remain multi-year.
Alabama local production, 765kV capability and integrated data-center power packages position the company in structural bottlenecks.
counter_evidence: Power equipment is cyclical and global capacity additions can eventually shorten lead times and weaken scarcity pricing.

evidence: Utilities and data-center customers value qualification, reliability, lead time, local manufacturing and bundled transmission/distribution supply.
The July Big Tech framework covers both power and distribution equipment, supporting package-level customer value.
counter_evidence: Framework maximum value is not equivalent to committed purchase orders, and large buyers retain negotiating leverage.

evidence: The company reports two consecutive years of U.S. extra-high-voltage transformer market leadership and reached its 1,000th U.S.-produced transformer in 2026.
Local U.S. manufacturing and 765kV expansion improve qualification and lead-time advantages.
counter_evidence: Market-share leadership is company-reported rather than independently reconstructed, and competitors are also adding capacity.
missing_data: Independent post-expansion market-share and pricing data.

evidence: TTM OCF is approximately KRW0.983T and mechanical OCF-minus-PPE about KRW0.671T on KRW4.337T revenue.
Strong backlog provides visibility for capacity utilization.
counter_evidence: Expansion capex is rising and project-level after-tax returns are not yet observable; advances and working-capital timing can flatter cash conversion.
missing_data: Post-ramp incremental NOPAT and invested-capital cohorts for Alabama and Ulsan.

evidence: Management has maintained selective high-margin order discipline while investing in local U.S. production and distribution capacity.
H1 orders already reached about 76.7% of the annual target without lowering stated profitability discipline.
counter_evidence: Large simultaneous expansions increase execution risk and their realized returns are not yet proven.

evidence: June deposits of about KRW1.010T materially exceeded company-defined borrowings of KRW114.5B.
The business remains strongly cash generative despite elevated expansion spending.
counter_evidence: Backlog execution requires working capital, guarantees and capex, and a sharp cycle reversal could consume cash even without solvency risk.

evidence: At KRW744,000, the retained Base value of about KRW651,003 is roughly 12.5% below price.
Retaining Base economics requires about 11.90% annual revenue growth in years 2-10 at a 10% required return after Base year-1 revenue of KRW5.2T.
counter_evidence: Backlog, pricing and structural grid demand make this growth path plausible enough that an outright unrealistic-bull-case rejection is not yet established.
missing_data: Normalized post-expansion owner cash margin and realized order pricing after industry capacity additions.

evidence: Retained Bull value is about KRW1.62M per share, more than 2.1x the reference price.
counter_evidence: Retained Bear value is about KRW206k, roughly 72% below price; the stock can suffer long-duration impairment even if the company remains profitable.

evidence: No material accounting or management-integrity impairment was identified in the reviewed audited FY2025 and H1 2026 filing evidence.
items.resolution_needed: Reassess immediately on audit, control, related-party or disclosure deterioration.

evidence: June deposits materially exceeded borrowings and internal cash generation supports the current expansion program.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor if capex or working-capital requirements materially outgrow internal cash.

evidence: No evidence reviewed indicates structurally excessive shareholder dilution.
items.resolution_needed: Continue tracking total shares, treasury stock and equity compensation.

evidence: Growth is supported by utility, grid-replacement and data-center equipment demand rather than disclosed marketing subsidies or customer financing.
items.resolution_needed: Track cancellations, advances and framework-to-purchase-order conversion.

evidence: Current margins and cash generation are strong, but Alabama and Ulsan expansion cohorts have not yet produced observable after-tax incremental returns.
items.resolution_needed: Measure post-ramp utilization, incremental NOPAT, cash conversion and invested capital versus the 10% hurdle.

evidence: Backlog growth, local U.S. scale and high-voltage product breadth do not show persistent moat contraction.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor lead times, pricing and share as competitor capacity expands.

evidence: The 10% hurdle reverse case requires about 11.90% annual growth in years 2-10 after a KRW5.2T year-1 revenue base; demanding for an industrial business but not demonstrably impossible given backlog and grid demand.
items.resolution_needed: Require either stronger normalized owner-cash evidence or a materially larger price discount before buy authorization.

evidence: NextEra represented 15.9% of H1 sales and no reviewed evidence shows a single customer or product dependence that is presently fatal; utility, Middle East, Europe, distribution and data-center channels provide diversification.
items.resolution_needed: Track top-customer concentration and Big Tech framework conversion.

evidence: Solvency risk is low, but valuation duration, cycle normalization and correlated capacity expansion can cause prolonged capital impairment if pricing and ROIC normalize.
items.resolution_needed: Validate post-expansion ROIC and obtain a clearer expectation gap relative to the 10% hurdle.

attacks: Global transformer and switchgear capacity additions shorten lead times and erase scarcity pricing.
AI data-center project financing tightens, delaying or cancelling equipment purchase orders.
The KRW1.1212T Big Tech framework headline overstates firm demand because actual POs are phased and conditional on build schedules.
NextEra or another large North American customer cuts orders after a capex cycle peak.
Copper, steel, tariff and logistics costs rise faster than contractual pass-through.
Alabama Plant 2 and Ulsan expansion ramp late or below utilization targets.
Customer advances and favorable working-capital timing reverse, weakening OCF despite accounting profits.
FX hedges protect near-term contracts but reduce upside or create timing volatility as KRW/USD moves.
Competitors with local U.S. capacity narrow qualification and lead-time advantages.
Mid-20s operating margin proves peak-cycle economics and normalizes toward the low-to-mid teens.

explicit_model_uncertainties: Firm PO conversion under the Big Tech framework
Normalized owner cash after advances and working capital
